decks.name: LeetCode #90 - Subsets II
decks.description: Generate all possible subsets of an array with duplicates without duplicate subsets

cards.question: Subsets II: Given an integer array nums that may contain duplicates, return all possible subsets (the power set). The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets. Return the solution in any order.

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.explanation: Use backtracking to generate all possible subsets, but store them in a set to automatically handle duplicates. Sort array first to ensure consistent tuple ordering. At each index, make two choices: include element or exclude it. When reaching end of array, convert current subset to tuple and add to set. Finally convert set of tuples back to list of lists. Set handles duplicate subsets automatically but uses extra space. O(n*2^n) time with set operations overhead.

solutions.name: Backtracking I
solutions.explanation: Use backtracking with intelligent duplicate skipping to avoid generating duplicate subsets. Sort array first to group duplicates together. At each index, first include current element and recurse. After backtracking, skip all consecutive duplicate elements before making exclude recursive call. This ensures we only process first occurrence of each duplicate value for the exclude branch. More efficient than set approach as it prevents duplicates rather than filtering them. O(n*2^n) time with better practical performance.

solutions.name: Backtracking II
solutions.explanation: Use loop-based backtracking similar to combination problems. Add current subset to result at beginning of each call (not just at base case). Use for loop to iterate through remaining elements starting from current index. Skip duplicates within loop by checking if current element equals previous and it's not first iteration. This naturally prevents duplicate subsets while exploring all valid combinations. Cleaner structure than binary-choice backtracking. O(n*2^n) time with elegant duplicate handling.

solutions.name: Iteration
solutions.explanation: Build subsets iteratively without recursion using smart duplicate handling. Start with empty subset. For each number, if it's not a duplicate, extend all existing subsets. If it is a duplicate, only extend subsets added in previous iteration (tracked by index). Use prev_idx to mark start of previous batch and idx to mark start of current extension. This ensures duplicates only create variations of subsets that already include previous occurrence. Most space efficient with O(1) extra space. O(n*2^n) time.
